title: fix(ui): reset view actions on route changes
body:
Resets client-managed `viewActions` when the active admin route changes. These are actions that are registered client-side via the `useActions` hook.

The problem is that TanStack Start preserves the `ActionsProvider` and only replaces the view-keyed subtree. So stale actions registered by the previous view could remain in the header after navigation. The fix is to pass the current view key to the `ActionsProvider`. When that key changes, the provider can reset its state and clear out any stale actions that were registered client-side.

The existing E2E tests cover this behavior when run against the TanStack Start framework.

title: feat: bundle payload skill into payload package
body:
Payload's agent skill now ships inside the `payload` npm package. The guidance an AI assistant reads matches the version of Payload a project has installed. The skill previously reached users only through a Claude Code plugin marketplace that tracks `main`. Guidance could describe APIs that a project's installed version does not have. Resolves PYLD-3360 `create-payload-app` no longer asks which assistant you use. It writes two files at the project root: ```md AGENTS.md # AI Agent For any Payload-related work, reference the skill at `node_modules/payload/skills/payload/SKILL.md`. ``` ```md CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md ``` Pass `--no-agent` to skip both. ## Key Changes - **Skill ships with the package** - The skill moved to `packages/payload/skills/payload/`. The package `files` allowlist now includes `skills`. - npm publishes the directory in the tarball. Consumers find it at `node_modules/payload/skills/payload/`. - **create-payload-app stops downloading the skill** - A `buildAgentConfigFiles` builder replaces the tarball fetch from GitHub. The generated files point into `node_modules`. - The `try`/`catch` around the download is gone. A failed local write now surfaces instead of degrading to a warning. - **The agent prompt is removed** - `select-agent.ts`, the `AgentType` union, and the `-a`/`--agent` flag are deleted. All three former choices produced identical content. - `--no-agent` is now the only opt-out. Runs passing `-a claude` will fail on an unknown flag. - **Marketplace entry retargeted** - `source` is now `./packages/payload`. The deleted `plugin.json` is inlined into the marketplace entry under `strict: false`. - The plugin entry no longer sets `version`. That field pinned the plugin and blocked updates. - **Docs and evals follow the move** - A new page, `docs/getting-started/ai-tooling.mdx`, covers both delivery channels. - The eval suite reads the skill from its new location. A spec now guards that path resolution. ## Design Decisions npm is the only channel that can version-match. Every marketplace variant serves whatever sits on `main`. Claude Code does not scan `node_modules`. A bundled skill stays invisible until something points at it. Consumers therefore add a pointer file. The cost is that the skill loses its frontmatter advertisement, the roughly 100 tokens Claude Code normally loads into the system prompt to make a skill self-triggering. An assistant will not surface it unprompted. The pointer names `SKILL.md` rather than the directory. `SKILL.md` opens with a table linking to specific anchors under `reference/`, so it acts as an index. Naming the directory instead leaves an agent to guess an entry point among twelve files. Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` and not `AGENTS.md`, so one file cannot serve every assistant. `CLAUDE.md` imports `AGENTS.md` rather than duplicating it, the interop pattern Claude Code documents. Editing `AGENTS.md` updates both. The marketplace plugin root is `packages/payload`. Claude Code's default scan of `/skills/*/SKILL.md` finds the skill without a `skills` field. Inlining the manifest into the marketplace entry avoids recreating a `plugin.json` inside a published npm package. Dropping the plugin entry's `version` is deliberate. A version string pins the plugin, and users receive updates only when that string changes. A stale local cache holding an empty `skills/` directory is what exposed this. Both channels expose a plugin named `payload`. Enabling both puts two copies at different versions in scope. The docs tell consumers to pick one. ## Overall Flow ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before ["Before"] A["GitHub main branch"] -->|"create-payload-app
downloads tarball"| B["project/.claude/skills/payload"] end subgraph after ["After"] C["packages/payload/skills/payload"] -->|"npm publish"| D["node_modules/payload/skills/payload"] D -->|"AGENTS.md pointer,
imported by CLAUDE.md"| E["AI assistant"] end ``` The skill used to arrive over the network at project creation, decoupled from the installed version. It now arrives with the dependency itself. ## References / Links - [Create and distribute a plugin marketplace](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces): marketplace entry fields, source types, and the default skill scan. - [How Claude remembers your project](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory): confirms Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` and not `AGENTS.md`, and documents the import pattern. - [npm package.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json): the `files` allowlist that controls tarball contents.

title: fix(drizzle): truncate PostgreSQL identifiers exceeding 63-char limit
body:
### What?

PostgreSQL identifiers exceeding 63 characters cause migration failures when combining nested arrays, localization, and versioning. Names like `_users_v_version_ingredient_sections_section_ingredients_locale_idx` (68 chars) get silently truncated by PostgreSQL, breaking subsequent migrations that reference the full name.

### Why?

Direct string concatenation in `traverseFields.ts` bypassed existing truncation utilities (`buildIndexName`, `buildForeignKeyName`), creating identifiers that exceeded the limit.

### How?

Applied truncation helpers consistently across all index and foreign key name generation:

**Array fields:**
- `${arrayTableName}_order_idx` → `buildIndexName({ name: ${arrayTableName}_order, adapter })`
- `${arrayTableName}_parent_id_fk` → `buildForeignKeyName({ name: ${arrayTableName}_parent_id, adapter })`
- Same for `_locale` indexes

**Block fields:**
- Applied to `_order`, `_parent_id`, `_path`, and `_locale` indexes
- Applied to `_parent_id` foreign keys

**Select fields:**
- Applied to `order`, `parent`, `locale`, and `value` indexes
- Applied to `parent` foreign keys

Helpers truncate to 60 chars (leaving room for suffixes like `_idx`, `_fk` and numbering for duplicates), ensuring compliance with PostgreSQL's 63-char limit.

Fixes #9649

title: fix(templates): guard realpath() in with-cloudflare-d1 isCLI check
body:
### What

One-character fix in [\`templates/with-cloudflare-d1/src/payload.config.ts\`](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/blob/main/templates/with-cloudflare-d1/src/payload.config.ts#L18) — add optional chaining to the \`realpath()\` return value before calling \`.endsWith()\`:

\`\`\`diff
-const isCLI = process.argv.some((value) => realpath(value).endsWith(path.join('payload', 'bin.js')))
+const isCLI = process.argv.some((value) => realpath(value)?.endsWith(path.join('payload', 'bin.js')))
\`\`\`

### When the bug surfaces

When the template is deployed unmodified to a Cloudflare Worker and any request hits the Next.js handler (e.g. \`GET /admin\`):

\`\`\`
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'endsWith')
\`\`\`

Every request returns HTTP 500 with the default Next.js error page; the error is not surfaced in Workers Observability, only in \`wrangler tail\`.

### Root cause

\`realpath\` is defined as \`(value) => fs.existsSync(value) ? fs.realpathSync(value) : undefined\` — so it returns \`undefined\` for paths that don't exist on the FS. On Workers, \`process.argv\` entries (e.g. \`'node'\`) don't resolve to real files, so \`realpath(value)\` is \`undefined\` and the subsequent \`.endsWith()\` throws. Locally (in \`pnpm dev\`) and during \`payload migrate\` this works because there is a real Node binary at \`process.argv[0]\`.

### Test

After applying this patch to the unmodified template and deploying to Workers, \`/admin\` returns 200 and the \"Create First User\" form renders correctly. Reproduced and verified on a fresh degit of [\`templates/with-cloudflare-d1\`](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/tree/main/templates/with-cloudflare-d1) at d6b2d73, Wrangler 4.61.1, Workers compat date 2026-05-16, Node 24.

The patched config has been running in production at https://cms.sutraelements.com/admin (private downstream repo at https://github.com/nickhaubner/sutraelements; the fix in our local copy lives in [src/payload.config.ts#L18](https://github.com/nickhaubner/sutraelements/blob/main/cms/src/payload.config.ts#L18)).

### Risk

Negligible — optional chaining only changes behavior when \`realpath()\` returns undefined, in which case the previous code would have thrown. All existing successful paths are unchanged.

title: chore(templates): fix with-cloudflare-d1 storage adapter registration
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the `with-cloudflare-d1` template so its R2 storage adapter is registered correctly when the template is installed with the currently pinned released Payload packages.

## Problem

The `with-cloudflare-d1` template was updated to use the newer top-level `storage` config key, but the template still pins released `3.82.1` Payload packages.

On that release line, storage adapters are still expected to be registered through `plugins`, not `storage`. As a result, the `r2Storage(...)` adapter in the template is not initialized.

That mismatch causes two user-facing failures:

- The admin UI crashes with `Functions cannot be passed directly to Client Components` because the unprocessed `storage` config leaks into the client config.
- The R2 storage adapter is not actually wired up, so generated import-map output and upload behavior are incorrect for the template.

## Solution

This change switches the `with-cloudflare-d1` template back from `storage: [...]` to `plugins: [...]` for the `r2Storage(...)` registration.

That keeps the template aligned with the released `3.82.1` runtime behavior it currently installs, while preserving the intended R2 integration.

## Impact

Users who create projects from `templates/with-cloudflare-d1` with the currently published package versions should be able to:

- start the app without the admin crash
- generate the import map correctly
- use the configured R2 storage adapter as intended

## Validation

- Reproduced the issue from the current template state before the fix by confirming the template used `storage: [...]` while pinning `3.82.1` packages.
- Verified the fix in the template source by updating the adapter registration to `plugins: [...]` and committing only that scoped template change.

## Related Issue

Fixes #17195
